one_line: Two blocking attribution errors anchor a day where frame repetition and historical-description takes need systematic repair.

findings.quote: OpenAI's AI found critical flaws threatening 70% of the web's servers
findings.instruction: The verification block marks this contradicted: the source credits Ryan Austin, a researcher at Calif, as part of the OpenAI programme — not OpenAI's AI alone. Wiz independently found the same bugs. Rewrite to reflect joint discovery, e.g. 'AI-assisted research found critical PHP flaws threatening 70% of the web's servers' or name both parties.

findings.quote: OpenAI's Patch the Planet programme used GPT-5.6 Sol to discover PHP2Shell
findings.instruction: The verification block contradicts sole AI attribution: the source credits a human researcher (Ryan Austin at Calif) working within the programme, with Wiz independently finding the same bugs. Rewrite to name the human researcher and clarify the AI-assisted role, e.g. 'OpenAI's Patch the Planet programme — with researcher Ryan Austin at Calif using GPT-5.6 Sol — discovered PHP2Shell; Wiz independently found the same bugs.'
The verification block marks this contradicted: the source says Kimi scored 55 and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 58 — a three-point gap, not one. Replace 'one point behind' with 'three points behind'.

findings.quote: Repo-level coding agents previously needed a cloud API; Flint runs the same workload locally on a Mac.
findings.instruction: The verification block flags this claim as unsupported: the source does not assert that repo-level coding agents previously required a cloud API. Either remove the 'previously needed a cloud API' framing or ground it in a source that supports the contrast.

findings.quote: Agent security enforcement previously ran on the host an agent controls.
findings.instruction: The take is a historical description, not a present-tense editorial position. 'It is now the case that agent security enforcement previously ran on the host' does not parse as a present-state claim. Rewrite to state what is now true, e.g. 'NVIDIA Sentry moves agent security enforcement off the host and into silicon the agent cannot reach.'

findings.quote: Before signing off on a banking agent, demand procedure-aware evals.
findings.instruction: Currents body must close on a presence-form maturity signal (what exists and what it is worth today), not a prescription. The imperative close belongs in Hands-On. Rewrite the final sentence to characterise the current state of the evidence, e.g. 'TauIndianBankBench is the first public harness to score both procedure and outcome on retail-banking tasks, and its gap figures are now on the record.'

findings.quote: Does your build-vs-buy calculus still hold at those margins?
findings.instruction: Big Picture body must close on a strategic question anchored to a specific role, decision, or constraint in the reader's org. 'Does your build-vs-buy calculus still hold at those margins?' is close but unanchored — it names no role or decision point. Sharpen to anchor it, e.g. 'If your infrastructure team is still quoting cloud-inference costs to justify managed services, do those numbers survive contact with DeepInfer's published margins?'

findings.quote: Credit underwriting previously required human analysts to read statements; Ramp's pipeline does it autonomously.
findings.instruction: The take restates the body's opening contrast rather than adding the position the body stopped short of. The body already establishes the before/after; the take should state the publication's editorial position on what this means, e.g. 'Autonomous credit underwriting is now a demonstrated production capability, not a roadmap claim.'

findings.quote: Local inference pipelines previously needed separate tools for speech and routing.
findings.instruction: Like c_612505817d3181da's take, this is a historical description rather than a present-state editorial position. Rewrite to state what is now true, e.g. 'A single Ollama update now covers text-to-speech and routing without leaving the local environment.'

findings.quote: Regulated enterprises previously had to trust managed AI vendors contractually; cryptographic proof now replaces that.
findings.instruction: Third instance of the 'X previously required Y; Z now replaces that' syntactic frame (also used in c_612505817d3181da and c_58935a3cd359327e takes). Three or more takes sharing a frame is a major pattern; flagged here on the third occurrence. Rewrite to break the frame, e.g. 'Cohere's attestation model makes the inference environment auditable, not just contractually promised.'

findings.quote: Regulated enterprises previously had to trust managed AI vendors contractually; cryptographic proof now replaces that.
findings.instruction: This is the third take in the issue using the 'X previously required Y; Z now replaces/does that' scaffold (also c_612505817d3181da: 'Credit underwriting previously required…'; c_58935a3cd359327e: 'Local inference pipelines previously needed…'; c_1d9ae1e097d3e864: 'Repo-level coding agents previously needed…'). Four takes sharing the same frame is a major finding. Rewrite this take and at least two others to break the repeated scaffold.

findings.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol uncovered two unauthenticated remote-code-execution bugs affecting servers running WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla.
findings.instruction: The digest sentence attributes sole discovery to GPT-5.6 Sol, but the verification block marks this contradicted: a human researcher (Ryan Austin at Calif) was the credited discoverer, with Wiz independently finding the same bugs. Rewrite to reflect joint/assisted discovery, e.g. 'AI-assisted research within OpenAI's Patch the Planet programme uncovered two unauthenticated RCE bugs in PHP, independently confirmed by Wiz.'

findings.quote: Each story today moves the same lever: something a financial-services firm previously accepted on trust now has a verifiable, auditable, or publicly benchmarked substitute.
findings.instruction: The synthesis frames all four Big Picture stories through a financial-services lens, but c_17e4b1b97e98586c (DeepSeek inference margins) and c_e1d58348124c25f7 (NVIDIA Sentry) are general infrastructure stories with no FS-specific angle in their bodies. The synthesis overfits the FS frame. Broaden to the actual cross-story pattern — verifiability replacing vendor trust — without restricting it to FS firms.

findings.quote: Map your highest-volume domain model's token distribution before the paper lands.
findings.instruction: The Hands-On imperative close must be sharpened to a specific artefact and trigger. 'Map your highest-volume domain model's token distribution' names no specific tool or artefact. Sharpen to name the VocabX script or Hugging Face tokeniser analyser and the trigger condition, e.g. 'Run VocabX's vocabulary-analysis script against your highest-volume domain model before the paper lands and the method gets packaged into a one-click tool.'

findings.quote: Quant AI deployments now have documented failure modes: benchmark collapse and adversarial fragility on the record.
findings.instruction: The colon construction ('documented failure modes: benchmark collapse and adversarial fragility') reads as a label rather than a single declarative sentence. Rewrite as a clean declarative, e.g. 'Quant AI deployments now have two documented failure modes — benchmark collapse and adversarial fragility — both on the public record.'

note: verdict rule: blocking >= 1 (A blocking finding is reputational or liability exposure, or a factual claim the issue cannot stand behind. One is enough; there is no volume at which it becomes acceptable.) | 2 echo(es) not counted: the same defect filed again in another field or under another criterion
